title.value: Halting Time is Predictable for Large Models: A Universality Property and Average-case Analysis
title.justification: This is the exact title mention at the start of the paper and in the metadata.
title.quote: Halting Time is Predictable for Large Models: A Universality Property and Average-case Analysis

extractions.description: The paper discusses the predictability and universality property of halting time in large-scale problems trained with first-order methods. It provides explicit average-case convergence rates and highlights that for almost all instances of high-dimensional data, the halting time is deterministic and independent of the probability distribution.

climate_change_is_central.justification: Although the paper explores deep learning and optimization methods that could indirectly be related to climate science, the core focus of the paper is mathematical and computational in nature, aimed at improving algorithm efficiency, rather than focusing on climate change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: In this paper, we analyze the halting time and develop the first explicit average-case analysis for first-order methods on quadratic objectives... It provides explicit average-case convergence rates showing a tighter complexity not captured by traditional worst-case analysis.

primary_category.justification: The potentially indirect relevance of this paper is its focus on algorithm efficiency which could, hypothetically, apply to climate models. However, no specific climate-related context is evident in the paper.
primary_category.quote: ...halting time is deterministic, the empirical complexity coincides almost surely with the average-case rates...Numerical simulations suggest this universality property holds for a more general class of algorithms and problems.
